keyChanges: react-i18next pinned to ~16.5.8 (tilde matches OCP 4.22 exactly)

issues.title: API Product deletion type to confirm missing when deleting from details

prSummary.problem: APIProduct detail page Actions dropdown used the SDK's built-in useDeleteModal for deletion, which shows a simple "Are you sure?" checkbox confirmation. The list page kebab menu already uses the custom type-to-confirm APIProductDeleteModal (enhanced in PR #609), creating an inconsistent delete experience across the two views.
prSummary.solution: Replaced useDeleteModal with the SDK's useModal hook to launch APIProductDeleteModal from the Actions dropdown, matching PatternFly design guidelines for "Confirm a destructive action". Detail page now navigates back to the APIProducts list after successful deletion.
keyChanges: onDeleteSuccess callback: Added optional prop to APIProductDeleteModal to distinguish successful deletion from cancel — detail page navigates away, list page behaviour unchanged
setIsDeleting cleanup: Moved out of finally block and into catch only, preventing React setState-on-unmount warnings when the modal is closed after deletion
Replaced useDeleteModal with useModal: Switched from the SDK's built-in delete confirmation to the generic modal launcher in useAPIProductActions

APIProductDeleteModalWrapper: Added wrapper component that bridges the Console ModalProvider API (closeModal prop) with APIProductDeleteModal, handling post-delete navigation to /kuadrant/apiproducts/ns/{namespace}
Updated delete confirmation flow: Test now types the resource name into #confirm-delete input instead of checking a checkbox, matching the new type-to-confirm behaviour

prSummary.problem: Header contents inside the DNS, TLS, and OIDC policy creation tabs were extremely left-aligned, mismatching the rest of the page layout.
prSummary.solution: Identified a PatternFly `pf-m-no-padding` modifier class applied to the body wrapper of each policy header. Commenting it out restored correct alignment across all three policy pages.
keyChanges: Commented out `pf-m-no-padding` class on DNS, TLS, and OIDC header wrappers
No logic changes — pure layout fix
Verified visually: headers now align with other page content

issues.title: Add GatewayClass filtering for gateway tables

prSummary.problem: Gateway tables displayed all gateways including irrelevant types like waypoint gateways (gatewayClassName: 'istio-waypoint'), adding noise to the UI. No filtering by GatewayClass existed — only Name, Namespace, and Type (resource kind) were available.
prSummary.solution: Extended ResourceList with a generic additionalFilters prop following PatternFly dropdown select patterns, keeping the component reusable for future filter needs. Wired up a GatewayClass dropdown filter in the "Gateways - Traffic Analysis" card on the Overview page, populated dynamically from cluster GatewayClass resources.
keyChanges: AdditionalFilter type: Defines a custom filter shape with label, options, and filterFn — fully decoupled from any specific resource
additionalFilters prop: Optional array defaulting to [], so all existing ResourceList callers are unaffected
Conditional toolbar rendering: When an additional filter is selected, the text input is replaced with a Select dropdown of available values plus an "All" default
Filter logic branching: The useEffect checks whether the active filter is an additional filter and uses its filterFn, otherwise the existing Name/Namespace/Type text matching runs unchanged
Gateway interface extended: Added spec.gatewayClassName for type-safe access during filtering
GatewayClass resource watch: Fetches all GatewayClass resources from the cluster using the existing RESOURCES.GatewayClass.gvk definition
gatewayClassNames memo: Extracts names from watched GatewayClasses into a string array for the dropdown options
additionalFilters prop: Passed to the Gateway ResourceList with a single "GatewayClass" filter that compares spec.gatewayClassName against the selected value

issues.title: Cancel button navigates to resource list instead of previous page

prSummary.problem: Cancel buttons on create/edit forms (policies, Gateways, HTTPRoutes — Form and YAML view) navigate to the resource list page instead of the previous page, breaking natural navigation flow.
prSummary.solution: Closed as not technically feasible. The OpenShift Console SDK's ResourceYAMLEditor does not expose an onCancel prop or any way to customise the cancel button. A custom YAML editor wrapper would be fragile and unnecessary given the planned form view work.
keyChanges: Custom YAML editor approach investigated and ruled out
Textarea alternative considered and discarded
Confirmed via SDK type definitions: cancel customisation is not supported
Same broken behaviour found on HTTPRoutes and Gateway YAML creation
Resolution deferred to upcoming form view redesign
